chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I love for the believer to remove unwanted hair every fifteen days.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.يَطَّلِيَ: to wax / to remove unwanted hair

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended frequency for removing unwanted hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi, narrated through a chain reaching Imam Ali (AS), establishes a specific rhythm for personal grooming, linking physical cleanliness (taharah) to spiritual purity. In Shia jurisprudence, this practice is often contextualized within the broader concept of 'fitrah' (natural disposition), emphasizing that regular maintenance of the body reflects inner discipline and readiness for prayer. The recommendation highlights the importance of self-care as an act of worship, ensuring that believers present themselves in a state of neatness and modesty.
